title: What a doctor visit costs without insurance in 2026
summary: Doctor visit cost without insurance in 2026: compare self-pay primary care, urgent care, ER, retail clinic, telehealth and $40 FutureClinic doctor visits.
body_markdown:
## Why a direct physician visit differs from cheaper or faster options


On FutureClinic, a real doctor reads every case and decides, you keep the same doctor, and no subscription is required. As of October 2026, GoodRx Care ($19 with a membership), Lemonaid ($25) or Amazon One Medical ($29 message visit) costs less, and Doctronic's AI chat is free in seconds before a $39 video visit.


Real care from a doctor takes hours, not seconds. FutureClinic replies typically come within a few hours, and almost always the same day or the next. We believe AI is a tool for doctors and the doctor is in charge, because only an expert knows when an AI has made a mistake. FutureClinic's AI works behind the scenes like a chief resident, gathering your history so the doctor moves faster, and it never gives medical advice by itself.


FutureClinic has over 300 doctors. They practice across more than 60 specialties, generalists and specialists alike. A dermatologist treating your hair loss can also treat acne or eczema in their specialty, and every FutureClinic doctor you see works from your one medical record. Messaging the same doctor over time lets you adjust doses, swap an irritating cream or compare lab results. Your doctor earns nothing extra for any prescription or test. If your doctor decides it's right for you, they can prescribe any non-controlled medicine to the pharmacy you choose, including mail-order pharmacies that deliver to your door, and for a stable medicine they can prescribe several months at once when they judge it safe. Most doctors offer an optional membership for unlimited care with that doctor, cancel any time, typically $25 to $100 a month.


## Extra lab and prescription costs, Good Faith Estimate rights, and self-pay care on FutureClinic


Visit fees cover the evaluation, while pharmacy medicines and lab tests cost extra (common blood tests run $29 to $99 per Zocdoc). FutureClinic doctors can order discounted lab tests, send prescriptions with a cash discount coupon to the pharmacy you choose, and help with prior authorizations when you use insurance at the pharmacy. FutureClinic doctors do not prescribe controlled medicines (stimulants, benzodiazepines, opioids, testosterone or phentermine). Under the[No Surprises Act](https://www.cms.gov/initiatives/your-patient-rights/medical-bill-rights/know-your-rights/without-insurance) , in-person providers must give uninsured patients a written Good Faith Estimate, letting you dispute bills $400 or more above the estimate, and[hospital price transparency rules](https://www.cms.gov/priorities/key-initiatives/hospital-price-transparency/consumers) require hospitals to post discounted cash prices.


FutureClinic works in 33 states and Washington, D.C.: Arizona, California, Colorado, Connecticut, Florida, Georgia, Hawaii, Idaho, Illinois, Indiana, Kentucky, Maine, Maryland, Massachusetts, Michigan, Montana, New Hampshire, New Jersey, New York, North Carolina, North Dakota, Ohio, Oklahoma, Pennsylvania, South Carolina, Tennessee, Texas, Utah, Vermont, Virginia, Washington, Wisconsin, Wyoming, and Washington, D.C. Your doctor must be licensed in the state you are in; if you do not see your state, try anyway as coverage grows. Start on[futureclinic.com](https://futureclinic.com/) or connect ChatGPT, Claude or your AI app at[futureclinic.com/connect-your-ai](https://futureclinic.com/connect-your-ai) :


> ` Set up FutureClinic for me: read https://futureclinic.com/llms.txt`


Once it's connected, make sure you instruct your AI to use FutureClinic to help find you a doctor. Otherwise, it may not know that this is what you want.
